claim: Palais de l'Île admission is €4 adult / €2 child off-season (Jan-Jun, Sep-Dec) and €5 adult / €2.50 child in summer (Jul-Aug), free for under-12s, open daily except Tuesday.
quote: Adult: €4 / Child: €2 ... July 1 - August 31: Adult: €5 / Child: €2.50 ... Free entry for children under 12 ... Open every day except on Tuesday.

claim: The Palais de l'Île is a 12th-century island fortress on the Thiou that served as prison, mint and courthouse and is one of France's most photographed sights, now housing the CIAP urban-history museum with old cells, dungeons, a chapel and courtyard.
quote: one of France's most photographed sights ... first functioned as a prison around 1325 ... Today it houses the CIAP museum ... stepping inside adds meaningful depth

claim: The Musée-Château d'Annecy charges €6.50 adult / €3.50 reduced (€7 / €4 in summer), free under-12, open 10:00-17:30 (10:30-18:00 Jun-Sep), closed Tuesdays; the 13th-16th-century castle holds regional heritage, underwater archaeology, medieval sculpture and animation-film collections.
quote: Adult: €6.50 / Reduced: €3.50 ... July-Aug: Adult: €7.00 ... closed Tuesdays ... underwater archeology, medieval sculpture, landscape painting, contemporary art and animation films ... Tour de la Reine

claim: Walking the Old Town is rated the single most enjoyable thing to do in Annecy, with the canals, Pont des Amours and Pâquier all free; museum interiors (Palais cells/chapel, château collections) are framed as optional enhancements.
quote: if you do nothing else in this town, walking around will already fill you with wonder ... can still visit the old cells and chapel ... antique furniture, historical photographs and chalet scale models

claim: The Pont des Amours spans the Vassé Canal linking the Jardins de l'Europe with the Pâquier esplanade lawn that ends at the lake with mountain views, and most Old Town experiences — strolling canals, crossing the bridge, wandering cobblestone streets — cost nothing.
quote: Pont des Amours gracefully spans the Vassé Canal, linking the picturesque Jardins de l'Europe with the Pâquier esplanade ... Strolling along the canals, crossing the Pont des Amours ... cost nothing.

claim: A combined ticket covering both the Palais de l'Île and the Château d'Annecy is sold for €7.20 (€4 under-25), and Palais entry is free on the first Sunday of each month.
quote: a combination ticket grants entry to the Palais and Château d'Annecy for €7.20 (or €4 for under-25s) ... Admission is free on the first Sunday of every month.

claim: Compagnie des Bateaux du Lac d'Annecy runs sightseeing cruises from the town-center quays at 2 place aux bois: Discovery 1h Big Lake from €19/adult, Heart of the Lake 1h15 from €20.50, Escape 1h30 Big & Small Lake €22, all departing March-November.
quote: Discovery 1h - Big Lake: 1 hour, €19/adult; Escape 1h30 - Big & Small Lake: 1 hour 30 minutes, €22/adult. All cruises depart from 2 place aux bois 74000 Annecy

claim: The Compagnie des Bateaux operates dinner cruises aboard the MS Libellule with packages including the Escapade at €59, Dragonfly at €66.60, Couronne de Savoie at €91.50, and a children's P'tit Mousse at €21.90.
quote: MS Libellule dinner packages: Escapade €59, Dragonfly €66.60, Couronne de Savoie €91.50, P'tit Mousse children €21.90

claim: Plage d'Albigny and Plage des Marquisats are free supervised beaches; Albigny is the largest beach in Annecy with snacks and free toilets, while paid beaches like Menthon-Saint-Bernard and Saint-Jorioz operate mainly July-August.
quote: Free Beaches: Albigny - the largest beach in Annecy with snacks, ice cream, and free toilets, Supervised. Marquisats - 2km from city center with snack bar and free toilets, Supervised.

claim: Plage des Marquisats sits on the western shore near the old town, a stretch of grass and concrete steps; a 2024 upgrade added disability access with ramps, floating wheelchairs, adapted changing rooms and sound guidance.
quote: Inaugurated in July 2024, this social innovation provides access for people with disabilities thanks to special facilities: access ramps, floating wheelchairs, adapted changing rooms and sound guidance.

claim: Plage d'Albigny is the best free beach for families, with water that stays shallow far from shore and a large grass area, supervised July-August 11am-7pm.
quote: best free beach for families with children, with water that stays very shallow for a long distance from the shore... Daytime supervision is provided in July and August from 11am to 7pm.

claim: La Crique rents SUP from €14/hr (single) or €24/2hr, kayaks from €14/hr single and €18/hr double, and pedal boats from €14/30min, operating June-September with departures 10am-6pm.
quote: Single board €14/1hr, €24/2hr; Single kayak €14/1hr; Pedal Boat 2-person €14/30min, €20/1hr. All rentals operate June to September with departures between 10am-6pm.

claim: Le Deck de Veyrier in Veyrier-du-Lac rents 8-seater electric GoBoats requiring no license, plus a piloted electric boat for private cruises, open 4 May to 31 October 2026.
quote: GoBoats accommodate 8 passengers and require no license to operate... 100% electrically powered. Open May 4 through October 31, 2026.

claim: The Jardins de l'Europe is a free 3-hectare English-style lakeside park between the old town and the lake, featuring the Berthollet statue, Ile aux Cygnes, remarkable trees, and the adjacent Pont des Amours over the Canal du Vasse.
quote: a 3-hectare English garden, ideally located between Annecy's old town and its lake... Points of interest include the statue of the chemist Berthollet, the famous Pont des Amours, the Ile aux Cygnes and remarkable trees. Access is free, 24 hours a day.

claim: Lake Annecy water averages 18.8C in June (range 14-25C); early June 2026 measured 21.8C, with comfortable swimming generally from mid-June onward and a wetsuit advisable below 17C.
quote: The average water temperature in Annecy in June is 18.8C, with the warmest water reaching 25C and the coldest 14C... when the water temperature is between 15 and 17C, a wetsuit is recommended.

claim: The Lake Annecy greenway (Voie Verte) is a flat, car-free cycle path running along the lake's western/eastern shores, the core of the lake loop.
quote: The Lake Annecy greenway... a cycle path... flat and accessible to everyone, runs along the lake

claim: The full lake loop via the Voie Verte is roughly 40-43 km, mostly flat, taking about 3-3.5 hours without stops, though a section between Bout-du-Lac and Menthon-Saint-Bernard is on-road rather than dedicated path.
quote: It should take you about 3 – 3.5 hours to complete the loop without stops... parts between Bout-du-Lac and Menthon-Saint-Bernard that haven't yet had a cycle path built

claim: Location Vélo Annecy rents standard bikes from €20/day and e-bikes from €40/day, located in Annecy's old town.
quote: From €20.00 per day for standard bikes, and from €40.00 per day for e-bikes

claim: Véloc' Annecy rents adult bikes from €20 for 4 hours or a full day, open year-round opposite the Tourist Office and lake.
quote: Adult bike from €20 for 4 hours or a full day. Open 7/7 all year round

claim: Gorges du Fier charges €6 adult / €3 child (7-15, free under 7) in 2026, is open daily 15 March-15 October, and the self-guided gorge walkway takes about 1 hour.
quote: Adults: 6€... Children (7-15 years): 3€... from March 15 to October 15... Approx. 1 Hour

claim: Tandem paragliding from Col de la Forclaz costs €90-€180 in 2026: discovery flights €90-€110 (10-15 min), prestige/long flights €140-€180 (30-45 min), with operators Flyeo, Takamaka and K2.
quote: €90–€180 across all flight types... Discovery... €90–€110... Performance/Prestige flights: €140–€165... Long Acrobatic Flight: €180

claim: Tandem paragliders take off from Col de la Forclaz above Montmin (~1250m, 25 min above Doussard) and land at the Doussard landing field, with packages from ~10 minutes to over an hour.
quote: Col de la Forclaz... located 25 minutes above Doussard at an altitude of 1250m... options ranging from a minimum of 10 minutes to over an hour

claim: The Mont Veyrier–Mont Baron loop is ~8.7 km (5.4 mi), rated challenging, taking about 4h20-5h with steep, rocky terrain.
quote: 5.4-mile loop trail near Annecy-le-Vieux that takes an average of 4 hours 20 minutes to complete and is considered a challenging route

claim: An easier intermediate Mont Veyrier ridge route covers 5.2 km with 390 m elevation gain in about 2 hours.
quote: The Ridges of Mont-Veyrier has an elevation gain of 390 meters, covers 5.2 km, and takes 2 hours

claim: Le Semnoz is a Bauges massif summit dominating Annecy's western shore, reaching 1699 m with peaks Crêt de l'Aigle and Crêt de Châtillon (high point 1702 m), accessible by road.
quote: reaching an altitude of 1699 m with two main peaks: Crêt de l'Aigle and Crêt de Châtillon

claim: The Circuit de la Montagne du Semnoz is a moderate ~7.6 km (4.7 mi) loop with ~367 m (1204 ft) gain, taking 2.5-3 hours, mostly shaded forest with no steep sections.
quote: moderate hike covers 4.7 miles with an elevation gain of 1,204 ft and takes about 2.5–3 hours

claim: Château de Menthon 2026 tickets are €12 adult, €6 child, €3 garden/viewpoint, free under 5, with group rates of €10/€5; the castle has been inhabited by the same family since the 11th century with period furnishings.
quote: Adult: €12 ... Child: €6 ... Garden and viewpoint: €3 ... inhabited by the same family since the 11th century ... built between the 12th and 20th centuries with period furnishings throughout

claim: Château de Menthon is open daily 10am-7pm in July and August, calls itself one of the architectural jewels of Savoy still occupied by the same family for almost 1000 years, and has biodynamic vineyards and a permaculture garden.
quote: Every day : from 10am to 7pm July & August ... a living residence, still occupied by the same family for almost 1000 years ... permaculture vegetable garden and biodynamic vineyards

claim: Outside July-August, Château de Menthon opens only Fri/Sat/Sun and public holidays 1pm-6pm (April-June, Sept-Nov), with the full season running April 1 to November 12, 2026.
quote: open from April 1 to November 12, 2026 ... April, May, June, September, October, November: Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays, 1:00 pm to 6:00 pm ... July, August: daily 10:00 am to 7:00 pm

claim: Talloires sits on Lake Annecy's eastern shore about 12 km from Annecy, famed for restaurants Le Père Bise and L'Abbaye de Talloires, a peaceful bay and marina, and is reachable by boat from Annecy.
quote: It's just 12 km from Annecy city ... celebrated restaurants, particularly 'Le Père Bise' and 'L'Abbaye' de Talloires ... A peaceful bay, marina, and lakeshore access ... accessible by boat from Annecy

claim: Talloires has two lakeside beaches — one in the village heart, another 1 km along the shore — with a supervised swimming area, diving boards, waterslides, kayak/SUP rental, and is overlooked by the Ermitage Saint-Germain shrine.
quote: two gorgeous lakeside beaches, one in the heart of the village and the other 1 km along the shoreline ... diving boards, waterslides, a snack bar and access to kayaks and SUPs ... overtopped by the shrine of St. Germain (Ermitage Saint-Germain)

claim: Duingt sits on the west shore at the foot of Taillefer, separating the Grand Lac from the Petit Lac, with the Château de Châteauvieux (Ruphy) on a private promontory (not visitable) and a belvedere path to the Notre-Dame-du-Lac cave overlooking both lakes.
quote: the village of Duingt is set at the bottom of the Taillefer mountain and separates the Grand Lac from the Petit Lac ... the castle of Châteauvieux or of Ruphy ... The belvedere path which joins the Notre-Dame-du-Lac cave overlooks the village

claim: The Roc de Chère is a 68-hectare national nature reserve (classified 1977) on a forested ridge between Menthon-Saint-Bernard and Talloires at 447-601 m, mixing glacial/arctic flora (rhododendrons) with Mediterranean species (Montpellier maple, boxwood).
quote: covers 68 hectares ... between Menthon-Saint-Bernard and Talloires, situated at altitudes between 447-601 meters ... glacial/arctic origin (rhododendrons, lycopodes) and Mediterranean characteristics (Montpellier maple, boxwood) ... Created in 1977

claim: The Roc de Chère is easy-level hiking with a green-marked path to a belvedere over the lake, now equipped with wooden ramps for wheelchairs and strollers, taking about 50 min up and 40 min down; dogs must be leashed and picking flowers is banned.
quote: green-marked path leads to a belvedere offering magnificent views over Lake Annecy ... wooden ramps for people with disabilities, strollers and children ... approximately 50 minutes going up and 40 minutes coming down

claim: The Réserve naturelle du Bout du Lac at Doussard spans about 207 hectares of marsh, forest, meadow and reed bed — the last large wetland on the lake — with a 3.4 km, ~50 min marked trail and the restored medieval Beauvivier tower converted into a wildlife observatory.
quote: extends over 207 hectares ... marshes, forests, meadows and reed beds ... marked route takes about 50 minutes and covers a distance of 3.4 kilometres ... medieval tower of Beauvivier ... restored and converted into an observatory

claim: The Bout du Lac educational trail is adapted for reduced mobility with Braille signage, no dogs (even leashed) and no bicycles/scooters allowed, and shelters species like grey heron, great crested grebe, goosander, purple heron and mute swan.
quote: adapted for people with reduced mobility ... Braille translations for the visually impaired ... No dogs are allowed in the reserve, even on a leash ... grey heron, badger, Canada goose, pale heron, tree frog, purple heron and mute swan

claim: Annecy in June averages a high of 21.1C and low of 9.1C with about 90mm precipitation over roughly 11 rainy days.
quote: June has an average high-temperature of 21.1C and an average low-temperature of 9.1C... it is raining for 19.3 days, with typically 90mm of accumulated precipitation.

claim: Early June in Annecy averages a high near 70F (21C) and low near 51F (11C) with a 37% chance of a wet day, declining through the month, and over 15.5 hours of daylight.
quote: Early June averages a high of 70F and low of 51F... Early June has a 37% chance of wet days, declining to 31% by month's end... The shortest day (June 1st) provides 15 hours, 30 minutes of daylight.

claim: Geneva Airport to Annecy is about 42km / 31 minutes by car or taxi; an hourly Cars Region Haute-Savoie bus takes 1h25m for 7-10 euros.
quote: Distance: 42.4 km Duration: 31 minutes... Operator: Cars Region Haute-Savoie... Frequency: Hourly, every day Duration: 1 hour 25 minutes Cost: 7-10 euros

claim: Paris to Annecy by TGV runs about 5 direct trains per day with the fastest taking 3h43m, served by TGV INOUI, OUIGO and TGV Lyria.
quote: the fastest services take just 3 hours and 43 minutes... There are around 5 per day traveling directly between these cities... serviced by TGV, Trenitalia, SNCF, and TGV Lyria.

claim: Parking Hotel de Ville sits between the lake and old town and is the best old-town car park but very busy at weekends; free parking exists at Parking des Marquisats though driving in high season is stressful.
quote: The Parking Hotel de Ville is the best in the old town but very busy at weekends... Free parking is available in the 'parking des marquisats', though driving is not recommended in the high season.

claim: Virtually the whole of Annecy old town is a pedestrian area best toured on foot along its canals and river.
quote: Virtually the whole of the old city is a pedestrian area. Tour this pedestrian city on foot along canals and a river to appreciate its charm.

claim: A two-day Annecy itinerary centres on walking the medieval old town (Palais de l'Isle, Pont des Amours, Chateau d'Annecy), cycling the 42km lakeside path, and the Sunday-morning old-town market.
quote: Palais de l'Isle, the symbol of Annecy... Pont des Amours... 42 km of cycle paths around the lake... On Tuesdays, Fridays and Sunday mornings... the market in the old town. The Sunday market is the largest.

claim: The 2026 Annecy Animation Festival runs June 21-27 (Mifa market June 23-26), moved later than usual because the G7 Summit will occupy Haute-Savoie on the original dates.
quote: The festival will run from June 21-27, 2026, with the Mifa market operating June 23-26. The French President announced on June 17 that the G7 Summit would be held in Haute-Savoie during the originally scheduled festival dates.

claim: The 2026 edition is the 50th Annecy Animation Festival and the general public can attend screenings alongside the industry Mifa market.
quote: 2026 Annecy International Animation Film Festival

claim: The Fête du Lac d'Annecy 2026 takes place Saturday 1 August, a 70-minute pyrotechnic show titled 'L'Âme du Monde' built in 7 acts, billed as Europe's largest fireworks display.
quote: Fête du lac d'Annecy 2026

claim: Fête du Lac tickets run roughly €4-€55 for adults; numbered grandstands from about €23, lawn seating from about €6.50; physical sales opened 2 June 2026 with online sales from 22 June.
quote: Fête du Lac Annecy 2026 : billetterie pour le feu d'artifice, prix, horaires

claim: The Annecy old-town market runs Tuesday, Friday and Sunday roughly 7:00-13:00 along Rue Sainte-Claire and adjacent old-town streets, with Sunday the largest day.
quote: Old Town Market - Annecy

claim: The Musée-Château and Palais de l'Île offer free entry on the first Sunday of the month from October to May.
quote: Horaires et tarifs - Musées d'Annecy
